title: The Weight of Qualification
text:
Scientific reports often contain qualifications that readers might initially mistake for indecision. A researcher who writes that a drug 'appears to reduce' symptoms is not hedging out of timidity; the phrasing reflects the limits of a particular sample. Such qualifications, when calibrated carefully, signal the strength of the evidence rather than the strength of the author's personal doubt.

Problems arise when qualifications are either excessive or absent. A text that hedges every sentence can obscure its own findings, leaving readers unsure which claims deserve attention. Conversely, a paper that presents tentative results with unqualified assurance may later appear reckless, particularly if subsequent studies fail to replicate its conclusions.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, why might a researcher write that a drug 'appears to reduce' symptoms?
options: Because the phrasing reflects the limits of a particular sample
Because the drug has no effect at all
Because journals require it in every sentence

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what might happen to a paper that presents tentative results with unqualified assurance?
options: It will always be accepted by journals

questions.text: What can be inferred about how readers should judge qualifications in scientific writing?
options: Every qualification is a sign of the author's ignorance
Qualifications should match the strength of the evidence
Qualifications should be ignored in favour of statistics
Texts without any qualifications are always more reliable

questions.text: What does the passage imply about a writer who hedges every sentence?
options: The writer has complete confidence in each claim
The writer may make it hard for readers to identify the key findings
The writer is likely to be cited more often
The writer has avoided any risk of being wrong

vocabulary.definition: limiting statements that narrow how far a claim applies
adjusted carefully so that something matches a standard or a level
to make something harder to see or understand
to repeat a study and obtain the same results

paragraph_translations: Наукові звіти часто містять застереження, які читачі спершу можуть сприйняти як нерішучість. Дослідник, який пише, що препарат, очевидно, зменшує симптоми, не ухиляється з боязкості; таке формулювання відображає межі конкретної вибірки. Такі застереження, коли їх ретельно узгоджено, вказують на силу доказів, а не на особисті сумніви автора.

Проблеми виникають тоді, коли застережень або надто багато, або їх немає зовсім. Текст, у якому кожне речення пом'якшене, може затьмарити власні результати, і читачі не розуміють, які твердження варті уваги. З іншого боку, стаття, що подає попередні результати з безумовною впевненістю, згодом може видатися необачною, особливо якщо наступні дослідження не зможуть відтворити її висновки.
